en: 5. The Section on Truths (Saccayamaka) 5.2 The Chapter on Occurrence (Pavattivāra) 5.2.2 The Chapter on Cessation (Nirodhavāra)
5.2.2.1 Present Section (Paccuppannavāra) 5.2.2.1.1 Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom the truth of suffering ceases,
does the truth of the origin cease for that person?
In all those passing away, and at the moment of the dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from craving during the course of existence,

the truth of suffering ceases for them, but the truth of the origin does not cease for them. At the moment of the dissolution of craving, both the truth of suffering and the truth of the origin cease for them.
Or rather, for whom the truth of the origin ceases, does the truth of suffering cease for them? Yes.
For whom the truth of suffering ceases, does the truth of the path cease for them?
For all those passing away, and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the path, the truth of suffering [ceases].

It ceases, but the truth of the path does not cease for them. In the five-aggregate realm, at the moment of the cessation of the path, both the truth of suffering and the truth of the path cease for them.
Or alternatively, for whom the truth of the path ceases, does the truth of suffering cease for them?
In the formless realm, at the moment of the cessation of the path, the truth of the path ceases for them, but the truth of suffering does not cease for them.
In the five-aggregate realm, at the moment of the cessation of the path, both the truth of the path and the truth of suffering cease for them.
Does the truth of the path cease for one for whom the truth of the origin ceases? No.
Or rather, for whom the truth of the path ceases, does the truth of the origin cease for that person? No.
5.2.2.1.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering ceases, does the truth of the origin cease there?
In the non-percipient beings, there the truth of suffering ceases … [as before] … (Wherever it is the same regarding arising, cessation, and both arising and cessation, there is no difference.
5.2.2.1.3. Positive Correlation: Person and Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
In whom, where, the truth of suffering ceases … [The "in whom and where" section should also be expanded in the same manner. 5.2.2.1.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
Does the truth of suffering not cease for one for whom the truth of origination does not cease? Yes.
Or rather, does the truth of suffering not cease for one for whom the truth of origination does not cease?
For all those passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from craving during the course of existence—for them, the truth of origination [does not cease].
It does not cease, yet for them the truth of suffering does not fail to cease. For all those being reborn,
during the moment of the arising of consciousness in the course of existence, and at the moment of the dissolution of the path and its fruition in the formless realm,
neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of suffering ceases.
For whom the truth of suffering does not cease, for them the truth of the path does not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of the path in the formless realm, for them the truth of suffering does not cease, but it is not the case that for them the truth of the path does not cease.
For all those being reborn, during the arising moment of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those in the fruit [of the path] in the formless realm...
At the moment of dissolution, neither the truth of suffering nor the truth of the path ceases for them.
Or conversely: for whom the truth of the path does not cease, does the truth of suffering not cease for them?
For all those passing away, and at the moment of dissolution of a consciousness dissociated from the path during the course of existence—for them, the truth of the path [does not cease].
It does not cease, yet for them the truth of suffering does not fail to cease. For all those being reborn,
during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and at the moment of the dissolution of the fruit in the formless realm,
neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering ceases.
For whom origination-truth does not cease, for them path-truth does not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of the path, for them origination-truth does not cease, but it is not the case that path-truth does not cease for them.
For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those whose consciousness is dissociated from craving and dissociated from the path...
At the moment of dissolution, for those who have attained cessation (nirodhasamāpanna) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta),

neither the truth of origination (samudayasacca) nor the truth of the path (maggasacca) ceases. Or, conversely, for whomsoever the truth of the path does not cease, for that person does the truth of origination not cease?
At the moment of the cessation of craving, the Truth of the Path does not cease for them, yet it is not the case that the Truth of Origin does not cease for them.
For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those at the moment of the cessation of a consciousness dissociated from the Path and dissociated from craving,
for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings— the Truth of the Path does not cease for them.
And the truth of the origin does not cease.
5.2.2.1.5. Negative Spatial Analysis:
Where the truth of suffering does not cease … [and so on] … pe … .
5.2.2.1.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what [place], the truth of suffering does not cease … [etc.
… (The "in whom" and "in what" sections are identical; however, in the "in whom and in what" section, the phrase "those who have attained cessation" must not be included.)
5.2.2.2. Chapter on the Past (Atītavāra) 5.2.2.2.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) has ceased, for that person has origination-truth (samudayasacca) ceased? Yes.
(Just as in the section on arising, the past questions were analyzed both in direct and reverse order, so too should they be analyzed in the section on cessation; there is no difference. 5.2.2.3.
Future Section 5.2.2.3.1.
Direct Person (Anuloma-puggala)
For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) will cease, for them origination-truth (samudayasacca) will cease?

For those possessing the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the supreme path—for these, suffering-truth will cease, but for them origination-truth will not cease. For others...
For those persons, both the truth of suffering will cease and the truth of the origin will cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever... [etc.]? Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering will cease, will the truth of the path cease for that person?
At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path (aggamagga), for Arahants and for those worldlings who will not attain the path,
the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) will cease, but the truth of the path (maggasacca) will not cease for them.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, for one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path, and for others who will attain the path...
For those persons, both the truth of suffering will cease and the truth of the path will cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever... [as before] ...Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of the origin will cease, will the truth of the path cease for that person? Yes.
For those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, the truth of the origin will cease, but the truth of the path will not cease for them. For those who will attain the path,
both the truth of the origin and the truth of the path will cease.
Or again, for whom the truth of the path will cease, will the truth of the origin cease for them?

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that thought-moment, the truth of the path will cease, but the truth of the origin will not cease for them. [This applies to] those who will attain the path.
For them, both the truth of the path will cease and the truth of the origin will cease.
5.2.2.3.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Wherever the truth of suffering will cease … [and so on] … pe … [as above].
5.2.2.3.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-puggalokāsa):
For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) will cease, for that person, there, origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) will cease?
[It will] for those possessing the supreme path (aggamagga-samaṅgī), for Arahants, and for one whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the supreme path.
For non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering will cease there, but the truth of origination will not cease for them there.
For others—those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—both the truth of suffering and the truth of origination will cease there. …pe…
(The same applies to whichever person and whichever base. 5.2.2.3.4.
Negative Person-Analysis:
For whom suffering-truth will not cease, for that person will origination-truth not cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom origination-truth will not cease, will suffering-truth not cease for them?
For those possessing the supreme path (aggamagga), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following [this moment] will attain the supreme path—
for these, origination-truth will not cease, but it is not that suffering-truth will not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, both the truth of origination and the truth of suffering will not cease for them.
For whom the truth of suffering will not cease, will the truth of the path not cease for that person? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom the truth of the path will not cease, will the truth of suffering not cease for that person? Yes.
At the moment of the cessation of the highest path (agga-magga), for Arahants and for those worldlings who will not attain the path,
the truth of the path (maggasacca) will not cease, but it is not the case that the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) will not cease for them. At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness,
for them both the truth of the path and the truth of suffering will not cease.
For whom origination-truth will not cease, for that person path-truth will not cease?

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness, origination-truth will not cease, but it is not the case that path-truth will not cease for them. [At the moment] of the supreme path...
At the moment of dissolution (bhaṅgakkhaṇa) for Arahants, neither the truth of origination (samudayasacca) nor the truth of the path (maggasacca) will cease.
Or rather: for whomsoever the truth of the path will not cease, for that person will the truth of origination not cease?
For those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path, the truth of the path will not cease; and yet [the truth of origination does not necessarily cease for them].
For them, the truth of origination will not cease. At the moment of the cessation of the highest path, for Arahants, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of origination will cease.
5.2.2.3.5. Negative Spatial Analysis (Paccanīka-okāsa).
Where the truth of suffering will not cease ... [as before] ... 5.2.2.3.6.
Negative Person-Space Formulation:
For whom, where the truth of suffering will not cease, will the truth of origin not cease there? Yes.
Or again, for whom and where the truth of origination will not cease, for that person and in that place will the truth of suffering not cease?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, for those whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the highest path,
and for non-percipient beings— for these, the truth of origination will not cease there, but it is not the case that for them the truth of suffering will not cease there.
It will not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for those persons, neither the truth of origination nor the truth of suffering will cease there.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering will not cease in a certain place, for that person the truth of the path will not cease in that place? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever the truth of the path will not cease at a certain place,
will the truth of suffering not cease for them there? For one at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, for Arahants, for those worldlings who will not attain the path,
and for those bound for the states of misery or non-percipient beings— the truth of the path will not cease for them there, yet it is not that the truth of suffering does not cease for them.

In that case, the truth of suffering will not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for those persons, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering will cease there.
For whomsoever the truth of origination will not cease in a certain place, for that person the truth of the path will not cease there either?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, origination-truth (samudayasacca) will not cease there;
yet it is not the case that path-truth (maggasacca) will not cease there for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, for Arahants and for non-percipient beings, both origination-truth and [path-truth] will not cease there.
It will not cease, and the truth of the path will also not cease.
Or rather: for whomsoever, wherever the truth of the path will not cease, for that person, there, will the truth of the origin not cease?
For those bound for the states of misery and for those worldlings who will not attain the path, the truth of the path will not cease there.

It will cease, yet for them, the truth of origination will not cease there. At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, and for Arahants and non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of origination will cease there.
5.2.2.4. Section on the Present and the Past.
5.2.2.4.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) ceases, for that person has origination-truth (samudayasacca) ceased? Yes.
Or rather, for whom origination-truth has ceased, for that person does suffering-truth cease?

For all those being reborn, for those during the life-continuum at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the cessation of the path and its fruition—
origination-truth (samudayasacca) has ceased for them, but suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not cease for them. For all those passing away,
and for those during the life-continuum at the moment of the cessation of consciousness— origination-truth has ceased for them.
And the truth of suffering ceases.
For whom the truth of suffering ceases, for that person had the truth of the path ceased?

For those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] at the moment of death, and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, the truth of suffering ceases.

And for them, the truth of the path had not ceased. For those who have realized the truths and are passing away, and at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, both the truth of suffering ceases and the truth of the path has ceased.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path has ceased, does the truth of suffering cease for them?

For those who have realized [the truths] at the moment of rebirth, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the dissolution phase of the path and the fruit—
the truth of the path has ceased for them, but the truth of suffering does not cease for them.
For those who have realized [the truths] at the moment of death, and during the dissolution phase of consciousness in the course of existence— the truth of the path has ceased for them.
And the truth of suffering ceases.
For whom the truth of origin ceases, for that person had the truth of the path ceased?

For those who have not yet fully realized [the truths], at the moment of the dissolution of craving, the truth of origin ceases for them; but for them, the truth of the path had not [previously] ceased.

The truth of the path has ceased. For those who have fully realized [the truths], at the moment of the dissolution of craving, both the truth of the origin ceases and the truth of the path has ceased.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path has ceased, does the truth of the origin cease for them?
For those who have realized the truths, at the moment craving arises, and for those whose minds are dissociated from craving or who have entered the attainment of cessation,

the truth of the path has ceased, but the truth of the origin does not cease. For those who have realized the truths, at the moment craving ceases, both the truth of the path and the truth of the origin have ceased.
5.2.2.4.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering ceases … [etc.
… 5.2.2.4.3. Positive Section: Person and Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) ceases, for them there has suffering-truth ceased at that place?

At the moment of dissolution of the rebirth-consciousness of those in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), suffering-truth ceases there, but for them origination-truth (samudayasacca) has not previously ceased there. For others, [this applies] to the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms.

In those who are passing away, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, both the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) ceases and the truth of origination (*samudayasacca*) has ceased there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever the truth of origination has ceased in a certain place, does the truth of suffering cease for them there?
For those being reborn in the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms, at the moment of the arising of consciousness during the course of existence, and for one on the path in the formless realm...
At the moment of the dissolution of the fruit [of action], origination-truth has ceased for those persons there,

but suffering-truth does not cease for them there. For those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence,
both origination-truth and suffering-truth have ceased and do cease there.
For whom and where does the truth of suffering cease, and for that same person and in that same place, had the truth of the path ceased?

For those in the pure abodes at the moment of the dissolution of the rebirth-consciousness, for those passing away who have not yet fully realized the truths, for those during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness,
and for those non-percipient beings at the moment of death— therein, for them, the truth of suffering ceases.

And yet, the truth of the path had not ceased for them there. For those who have realized [the truths] at the moment of death or during the subsistence phase of consciousness, the truth of suffering ceases and the truth of the path has also ceased there.
Or rather: for whomsoever the truth of the path has ceased there, does the truth of suffering cease for that person there?

For those who have realized [the truths] at the moment of rebirth, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the dissolution phase of the path and its fruition—
path-truth has ceased for them there, but suffering-truth does not cease for them there.
For those who have realized [the truths] at the moment of death, and during the dissolution phase of consciousness in the course of existence— for them there...
The truth of the path has ceased, and the truth of suffering is ceasing.
For whom, wherever, the truth of origin ceases, for that person, there, has the truth of the path ceased?
In those who have not yet fully realized [the truths], at the moment of the dissolution of craving, for them, there, the truth of origin ceases; [but] it has not [ceased].

And for those persons, the truth of the path had ceased there. For those who have fully realized [the truths] at the moment of the dissolution of craving, both the truth of the origin ceases and the truth of the path has ceased there.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path had ceased there, does the truth of the origin cease for that person there?
For those who have already realized [the truths], at the moment craving arises, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring,

the truth of the path has ceased for them there, but the truth of the origin does not cease for them there. For those who have already realized [the truths], at the moment craving ceases, both the truth of the path and the truth of the origin have ceased for them there.
5.2.2.4.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) does not cease, for that person has origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) not ceased? It has ceased.
Or else, for whom origination-truth has not ceased, for that person does suffering-truth not cease? There is none.
For whom suffering-truth does not cease, for them has path-truth not ceased?

For those who have already realized [the truths] at the moment of rebirth, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the ceasing phase of both the path and its fruit—
for these, suffering-truth does not cease, but it is not the case that path-truth has not ceased for them.
For those who are not yet enlightened and are being reborn, and for those during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence,
the truth of suffering does not cease and the truth of the path has also not ceased.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path has not ceased, does the truth of suffering not cease for them?
For those who have not yet attained realization and are passing away, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence,

the truth of the path has not ceased for them, but the truth of suffering does not fail to cease for them. For those who have not yet attained realization and are being reborn, and at the moment of the arising of consciousness during the course of existence, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering has ceased for them.
For whom origination-truth does not cease, for them path-truth has not ceased?

For those who have already realized [the truths], at the moment craving arises, when a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for those who have attained cessation— for them origination-truth does not cease, but it is not the case that path-truth has not ceased for them. For those who have not yet realized [the truths]...
At the moment of the arising of craving, when a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings,
neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of the path has ceased. Or, conversely, for whom the truth of the path has not ceased, does the truth of the origin not cease for them?
For those who have not yet attained realization, at the moment craving ceases, the truth of the path has not ceased for them,
but the truth of the origin does not fail to cease for them. For those who have not yet attained realization, at the moment craving arises,
or while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, or in the case of non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin has ceased for them.
5.2.2.4.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering does not cease … [etc. … 5.2.2.4.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not cease, for them there, origination-truth (samudayasacca) has not ceased?

For those being reborn in the four- or five-aggregate realms, during the arising-moment of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the ceasing-moment of the Path and the Fruit—therein, for them, suffering-truth does not cease; yet for them, [origination-truth has not ceased].

In that case, the truth of origination had not ceased. At the moment of the arising of the rebirth-consciousness of those born in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), and for those beings being reborn among the non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), neither the truth of suffering nor the truth of origination has ceased there.
Or rather: for whomsoever the truth of origination had not ceased in a certain place, does the truth of suffering not cease for him in that same place?

At the moment of dissolution of the rebirth-consciousness of the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), origination-truth (samudayasacca) had not ceased there,
but suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not fail to cease there for them. At the moment of arising of the rebirth-consciousness of the Pure Abodes,
and for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings, origination-truth had not ceased there for them either.
And the truth of suffering does not cease.
For whom, where the truth of suffering does not cease, for that person there, did the truth of the path not cease?

[It did not cease] for those who have already realized [the truths], for those being reborn, during the arising moment of consciousness in the course of existence, and in the formless realm, for both the path and the fruit.
And at the moment of dissolution, suffering-truth does not cease for them there, yet path-truth has not failed to have ceased for them there.
For those in the state of rebirth-consciousness of the Pure Abodes, for those being reborn who have not yet fully realized the truths,

for those during the arising-moment of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings— at these times, suffering-truth [does not cease] for them there.
The truth of the path does not cease, nor has it ceased.
Or rather: for whomsoever, wherever the truth of the path has not ceased, for that person there the truth of suffering does not cease?

[It does not cease] at the moment of dissolution of the rebirth-consciousness of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), nor in those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] while passing away during the course of existence (pavatta).

At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those passing away from the non-percipient beings, the truth of the path has not ceased there, yet the truth of suffering does not fail to cease there.

At the moment of the arising of the rebirth-consciousness of pure-abode beings; at the moment of the arising of consciousness during the course of existence for those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] while being reborn; and for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings.
For them, in that case, neither the truth of the path has ceased nor does the truth of suffering cease.
For whomsoever the truth of the origin does not cease in a certain place, for that person has the truth of the path not ceased there?
[Answer: For those who have already realized the truths, at the moment of the arising of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, for them in that case...
The truth of origination does not cease, yet the truth of the path has not ceased for them there.

For those in the second moment of consciousness of the Pure Abodes; for those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] at the moment of the arising of craving; for those whose minds are dissociated from craving while it is occurring;
and for non-percipient beings—for these, neither the truth of origination nor the truth of the path has ceased there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever the truth of the path has not ceased at a certain place, does the truth of the origin not cease for them there?

For those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] at the moment of the dissolution of craving, the truth of the path has not ceased there, but it is not the case that the truth of the origin does not cease for them there.
This is also the case when the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) is occurring.

For those who have not yet attained realization, at the moment craving arises, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings—therein, neither the truth of the path has ceased nor does the truth of the origin cease.
5.2.2.5. Chapter on the Present and Future.
5.2.2.5.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom the truth of suffering ceases, will the truth of origin cease for that person?

At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants, and for whichever consciousness immediately follows [the death-moment], [the truth of origin will cease].
At the moment of the cessation of that consciousness in those who will attain the supreme path, the truth of suffering ceases for them,
but the truth of origination will not cease for them. For others at the moment of death and during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness,
both the truth of suffering ceases and the truth of origination will cease.
Or, for whom origination-truth will cease, for them suffering-truth ceases? For all those being reborn,
during the arising-moment of consciousness in the course of existence, and at the cessation-moment of the path and the fruit in the immaterial realm—
for these, origination-truth will cease, but suffering-truth does not cease for them.
For all those passing away and for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence,
both the truth of origination will cease and the truth of suffering is ceasing.
For whom the truth of suffering is ceasing, will the truth of the path cease for them?
At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path, at the moment of the cessation of the consciousness of Arahants,

and for those worldlings who will not attain the path at the moment of their death or during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness— suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) ceases for them,
but path-truth (maggasacca) will not cease for them. [This applies] to that consciousness immediately after which the supreme path...

At the moment of the cessation of that consciousness, and for others who will attain the path at the moment of death or during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, both the truth of suffering ceases and the truth of the path will cease.
Or rather: for whomsoever the truth of the path will cease, does the truth of suffering cease for them?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path,
in others who will attain the path, in those being reborn, during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness,
and in the formless realm at the moment of the dissolution of both the path and its fruit— for these, the truth of the path (maggasacca) exists.
[The path-truth] will cease, but the truth of suffering does not cease for them.
At the moment of dissolution of that consciousness immediately before those who will attain the supreme path, and for others who will attain the path at the time of death,
as well as during the course of existence at the moment of dissolution of consciousness— for these, both the path-truth will cease and the truth of suffering ceases.
For whom the truth of the origin ceases, will the truth of the path cease for them?

For those worldlings who will not attain the path, at the moment of the dissolution of their craving, the truth of the origin ceases, but the truth of the path will not cease for them. For those who will attain the path...
At the moment of the destruction of craving, both the truth of the origin (*samudayasacca*) ceases and the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) will cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will cease, does the truth of the origin cease for that person?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (*aggamagga*), for one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path, and for others as well...
For those who will attain the path, at the moment craving arises, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring,
and for those who have entered cessation or are non-percipient beings, the truth of the path will cease, but the truth of the origin does not cease for them.
For those who will attain the path, at the moment craving ceases, for them both the truth of the path and...
It will cease, and the truth of the origin also ceases.
5.2.2.5.2. Positive Plane:
Where the truth of suffering ceases … [and so on] … pe … .

5.2.2.5.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what place, does the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) cease, and will the truth of the origin (samudayasacca) cease for that person in that same place?

At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants, and in relation to whichever consciousness immediately follows [the attainment of Arahantship]...
At the moment of the cessation of that consciousness in those who will attain the supreme path, and in those non-percipient beings at the moment of death, suffering-truth ceases there;

but origination-truth will not cease there for them. For others—those passing away from the four- or five-aggregate states—at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, [suffering-truth ceases there].
Does the truth of suffering cease and the truth of origination cease?
Or, conversely, for whomsoever and wherever the truth of origination will cease, does the truth of suffering cease for that person there?
[It ceases] for those being reborn in the four- or five-aggregate realms, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those on the path in the immaterial realm.
At the moment of dissolution of the fruit [of kamma], origination-truth will cease for them there,
but suffering-truth does not cease for them there. For those passing away from the four- or five-aggregate planes at the moment of dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence,
both origination-truth and suffering-truth cease there.
For whom and where does the truth of suffering cease, will for them there the truth of the path cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path; at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants; in the case of those bound for the states of misery;

and in the case of those worldlings who will not attain the path, at the moment of their death and during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness; [and] in the case of non-percipient beings.
For those passing away there, the truth of suffering ceases there, but the truth of the path will not cease for them there.
At the moment of dissolution of that consciousness immediately preceding the attainment of the highest path (aggamagga),

and for others who will attain the path, as well as for those passing away during the life-continuum at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness— for these, [the truth of suffering ceases, but the truth of the path will not cease].
In that case, does the truth of suffering cease and the truth of the path also cease?
Or, conversely, for whomsoever the truth of the path will cease in a certain place, does the truth of suffering cease for them in that same place?

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for that consciousness immediately following which one will attain the supreme path—[for such a person, the truth of suffering ceases].
At the moment of arising of consciousness for those who will attain the path, for those being reborn, during the course of existence at the moment of arising of consciousness,
and for those in the formless realm at the moment of dissolution of the path and its fruit— therein, the truth of the path will cease for them,
but the truth of suffering does not cease for them. Immediately after that consciousness...
At the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness when they will attain the supreme path (aggamagga),
and for others who will attain the path at the moment of death or during the subsistence phase of consciousness at the moment of its dissolution— for them, there,
the truth of the path (maggasacca) will cease and the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) ceases.
For whom and where the truth of the origin ceases, for them will the truth of the path cease there?
For those bound for the states of deprivation and for those worldlings who will not attain the path— at the moment of the cessation of their craving—
the truth of the origin ceases for them there, but the truth of the path will not cease for them there.
For those who will attain the path, at the moment of the dissolution of craving, both the truth of origination ceases and the truth of the path will cease there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever the truth of the path will cease in a certain place, does the truth of origination cease for that person in that same place?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), in the case of those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness,
and in the case of others who will attain the path, at the moment of the arising of craving and while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring,
the truth of the path (maggasacca) will cease therein for them, but the truth of the origin (samudayasacca) does not cease therein for them.
For those who will attain the path, at the moment of the dissolution of craving, both the truth of the path and the truth of the origin will cease there. 5.2.2.5.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom suffering-truth does not cease, for them will origination-truth not cease? For all those being reborn,
during the arising-moment of consciousness in the course of existence, and at the ceasing-moment of the path and the fruit in the immaterial realm—
for these, suffering-truth does not cease, yet it is not the case that origination-truth will not cease for them.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants,

at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, and at the moment of the dissolution of both the supreme path and its fruition (phala) in the formless realm (arūpa)—
for these persons, neither the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) has ceased nor will the truth of origination (samudayasacca) cease.
Or rather, for whom origination-truth (samudayasacca) will not cease, does suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) not cease for them?
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants,
and at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path— for these, origination-truth will not cease.
And yet, the truth of suffering does not cease for them. For those at the moment of the arising of the supreme path, for Arahants at the moment of the arising of consciousness,
for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness at the moment of its arising,
and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the dissolution of both the supreme path and its fruition— the truth of the origin does not cease for them.
And the truth of suffering does not cease.

For whom the truth of suffering does not cease, will the truth of the path not cease for them? At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path—for such a person [the truth of suffering does not cease, yet the truth of the path will not cease].
At the moment of arising of the consciousness of those who will attain the path, at the moment of rebirth of those [beings] being reborn,
during the course of existence at the moment of arising of the consciousness, and at the moment of dissolution of the path and the fruit in the formless realm—

for these, the truth of suffering does not cease, yet it is not the case that the truth of the path will not cease for them. This is also the case at the moment of arising of the consciousness of Arahants.
And for those worldlings who will not attain the path, at the moment of their rebirth-linking, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence,
and at the cessant phase of the highest path and its fruition in the formless realm— for these,
neither the truth of suffering has ceased nor will the truth of the path cease.
Or rather, for whom path-truth will not cease, for that person does suffering-truth not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path; at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants;

and for those worldlings who will not attain the path, at the moment of their death and during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness—for these, path-truth [will not cease].
It will not cease, yet the truth of suffering does not fail to cease for them. For Arahants at the moment of the arising of consciousness;
for those ordinary persons who will not attain the path at the moment of rebirth; during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness;
and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path and its fruit—for these, neither the truth of the path nor [the truth of suffering] ceases.
[The truth of suffering will cease, but the truth of suffering does not cease.
For whom the truth of origination does not cease, will the truth of the path not cease for them?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for one who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, and for others...

For those who will attain the path, at the moment craving arises, for those whose minds are dissociated from craving, and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings—craving-truth does not cease for them;
yet it is not the case that path-truth will not cease for them. [This is also true] at the moment of the destruction of the supreme path, for Arahants and for those worldlings...
For those who will not attain the path, at the moment of the arising of craving while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring,
neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of the path ceases. Or, for whomsoever the truth of the path will not cease, does the truth of the origin not cease for them?
For those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, at the moment of the dissolution of their craving, the truth of the path will not cease;
yet it is not the case that the truth of the origin does not cease for them.
[This is also the case] at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, for Arahants and for those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, at the moment of the arising of their craving.
When a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, for those [beings], the truth of the path will not cease and the truth of the origin does not cease.
5.2.2.5.5. Negative Plane:
Where the truth of suffering does not cease …pe…

5.2.2.5.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what [plane], the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) does not cease, will the truth of origin (samudayasacca) not cease for them there?

[It will not cease] in those being reborn in the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms; during the course of existence (pavatta), at the moment of the arising of consciousness; and in the formless realm (arūpa), at the moment of the arising of the Path (magga).
At the moment of the cessation of the fruit, suffering-truth does not cease for those persons at that location,
yet origination-truth will not fail to cease for them there. At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants,
and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the supreme path— [origination-truth will not cease].

For those beings reborn in the non-percipient realm (asaññasatta), and for those at the moment of the cessation of the path and its fruit in the formless realm (arūpa), suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not cease there, nor will origination-truth (samudayasacca) cease. Or conversely:
for whomsoever origination-truth will not cease in a certain place, does suffering-truth not cease for them in that same place?

At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, at the moment of the dissolution of the minds of Arahants, at the moment of the dissolution of that mind immediately after which they will attain the supreme path,
and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings— therein, the truth of the origin will not cease, but it is not the case that the truth of suffering does not cease for them therein.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants,

at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path, at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path and its fruition in the formless realm,
and for those being reborn in the sphere of non-percipient beings— among these, the truth of origination (samudayasacca) will not cease there.
And the truth of suffering does not cease.
For whom, where the truth of suffering does not cease, will the truth of the path not cease for them there?

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path—for such a person, [the truth of the path will not cease].
At the moment of arising of consciousness in those who will attain the Path, in those being reborn, during the course of existence at the moment of arising of consciousness,
and in the immaterial plane at the moment of dissolution of the Path and its Fruit— suffering-truth does not cease there for them,
yet path-truth will not fail to cease there for them. [In the case] of Arahants, at the moment of arising of consciousness...
At the moment of arising for those destined for the states of misery, for those worldlings who will not attain the path when they are reborn,

during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those being reborn in the non-percipient realm, and at the moment of the dissolution of the highest path and its fruit in the formless realm—
for these persons, in those cases, the truth of suffering does not cease, and the truth of the path will not cease.
Or conversely: For whom, and where, the truth of the path will not cease, for that person there, does the truth of suffering not cease?
[It does not cease] at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path; at the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness of Arahants; in the case of those bound for the states of misery;

and in the case of those worldlings who will not attain the path, at the moment of their death and during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness; and in the case of non-percipient beings.
For those who are passing away there, the truth of the path will not cease there; yet it is not that the truth of suffering does not cease for them there.

[This is the case] for Arahants at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those bound for the states of deprivation, for those worldlings who will not attain the path, for those being reborn, during the moment of the arising of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the supreme path.
And at the moment of the dissolution of the fruit, for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings,
the truth of the path will not cease there and the truth of suffering does not cease there.
For whom, where the truth of origination does not cease, for that person there, will the truth of the path not cease?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), in the case of those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness,
and in the case of others who will attain the path, at the moment of the arising of craving while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring—
therein, the truth of the origin does not cease for them, yet it is not the case that the truth of the path will not cease for them therein.
At the moment of the destruction of the supreme path, for Arahants, for those destined for the states of misery,
and for those worldlings who will not attain the path— at the moment craving arises, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring,
and for non-percipient beings— therein the truth of the origin does not cease, and the truth of the path will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever the truth of the path will not cease at a certain place, does the truth of the origin not cease for them there?
For those born in the states of misery (āpāyika) and for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path— at the moment of the dissolution of their craving—
the truth of the path will not cease for them there, but it is not the case that the truth of the origin does not cease for them there.
At the moment of the destruction of the supreme path, for Arahants, for those bound for the states of misery, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path at the moment craving arises,
while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring,
and for non-percipient beings— therein the truth of the path will not cease, and the truth of the origin does not cease.
5.2.2.6. Chapter on the Past and Future (Atītānāgatavāra) 5.2.2.6.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) has ceased, will origination-truth (samudayasacca) cease for that person?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path,
the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) has ceased, but the truth of origination (samudayasacca) will not cease for them.
For others, both the truth of suffering has ceased and the truth of origination will cease.
Or again, for whomsoever... [as before] ...? Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering has ceased, will the truth of the path cease for him?
At the moment of the dissolution of the highest path (agga-magga), and for those Arahants, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path.
For them, the truth of suffering has ceased, but the truth of the path will not cease for them.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for one who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, and for others who will attain the path,
both the truth of suffering has ceased and the truth of the path will cease.
Or again, for whomsoever... [as before] ...? Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of the origin has ceased, will the truth of the path cease for him?
At the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (agga-magga), for Arahants, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path.
For them, the truth of origination has ceased, but the truth of the path will not cease for them.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, and for others who will attain the path,
both the truth of origination has ceased and the truth of the path will cease.
Or, for whom... [etc.]? Yes. 5.2.2.6.2.
Positive Plane: Where the truth of suffering has ceased... [etc.]...

5.2.2.6.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-puggalokāsa) In whom, and in what place, has the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) ceased, will the truth of origination (samudayasacca) cease for that person in that same place?
[It will cease] in those who possess the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), in Arahants, and in those whose consciousness immediately following [this moment] will attain the supreme path.
For non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering has ceased there, but the truth of origination will not cease for them there.
For others— those of the four-constituent and five-constituent realms— both the truth of suffering and the truth of origination have ceased and will cease there.
Or conversely: for whomsoever origination-truth will cease at a certain place, has suffering-truth ceased for them there?
For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), origination-truth will cease there, but suffering-truth has not ceased for them there.
For others—those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—it is as follows: [origination-truth will cease, and suffering-truth has also ceased].
The truth of origination will cease and the truth of suffering has ceased.
For whom, where the truth of suffering has ceased, will the truth of the path cease there?
[It will not cease] at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path (agga-magga), nor for Arahants, nor for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path.
For those in the states of misery and for non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering has ceased there, but the truth of the path will not cease there for them.
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for one who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness,
and for others who will attain the path, both the truth of suffering and [the truth of the path] have ceased there.
And the truth of the path will cease.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever the truth of the path will cease, has the truth of suffering ceased for them there?
For those beings being reborn in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), the truth of the path will cease there, but the truth of suffering has not ceased for them there.
The truth of suffering has ceased. At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness,
and for others who will attain the path, there both the truth of the path will cease and the truth of suffering has ceased.
For whom, where origination-truth has ceased, will path-truth cease there?
At the moment of the destruction of the supreme path, for Arahants, for those worldlings who will not attain the path,
and for those bound for the states of misery— origination-truth has ceased for them there, but path-truth will not cease for them there.

It will cease. At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness, and for others who will attain the path, there both the truth of origination has ceased and the truth of the path will cease.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will cease at a certain place, for that person the truth of origination has ceased at that place.
When the second consciousness of the Suddhāvāsa deities is occurring, the truth of the path will cease for them there,
but the truth of the origin has not ceased for them there. At the moment of the arising of the highest path (aggamagga),
for those who will attain the highest path immediately after that consciousness, and for others who will attain the path, [the truth of the path will cease] there.
The truth of the path will cease, and the truth of the origin has ceased.
5.2.2.6.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala):
For whom the truth of suffering has not ceased, will the truth of the origin not cease for them? None.
Or, for whom origination-truth (samudayasacca) will not cease, has suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) not ceased for them? It has ceased.
For whom suffering-truth has not ceased, will path-truth (maggasacca) not cease for them? There is none.
Or, for whom path-truth will not cease, has suffering-truth not ceased for them? It has ceased.
For whom origination-truth had not ceased, for that person path-truth will not cease? None.
Or rather, for whom path-truth will not cease, for that person origination-truth had not ceased? It had ceased.
5.2.2.6.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where the truth of suffering has not ceased... [etc. 5.2.2.6.6.
Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa):
For whom, where the truth of suffering has not ceased, will the truth of the origin not cease there? It will cease.
Or rather, for whom origination-truth will not cease at a certain place, has suffering-truth not ceased there for them? It has ceased.
For whom suffering-truth has not ceased at a certain place, will path-truth not cease there for them? It will cease.
Or rather, for whom path-truth will not cease at a certain place, has suffering-truth not ceased there for them? It has ceased.
For whom, where origination-truth has not ceased, for them there will not cease path-truth there?

For those in the second moment of consciousness among the Pure Abodes, origination-truth has not ceased there, yet path-truth will not fail to cease there for them. For non-percipient beings, both origination-truth and...
The truth of the path has not ceased, and it will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever the truth of the path will not cease at a certain place, has the truth of the origin not ceased for them there?
[It has] for one at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path, for Arahants, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path.
For those destined for the states of misery, the truth of the path will not cease there, but the truth of the origin has not [previously] ceased for them there.
For non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin will cease there.
The Chapter on Cessation.
